_note: Pest & disease reference used to ground AI diagnoses and to power the offline symptom matcher. Chemical options are listed as active ingredients; always use products registered in the farmer's country, follow the label, wear protection and respect pre-harvest intervals. Integrated pest management first.

pests.symptoms: Ragged holes and 'window panes' on young leaves, wet sawdust-like frass in the leaf whorl, caterpillars with an inverted Y on the head and four dots in a square near the tail.
cultural: Scout 20 plants in a W pattern twice a week from emergence
Hand-pick and crush egg masses and caterpillars
Intercrop with desmodium and border with brachiaria/napier (push-pull)
Plant early and at the same time as neighbours
biological: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) sprays into the whorl
Protect natural enemies (earwigs, ants, parasitic wasps)
chemical: Emamectin benzoate
Spinetoram
Chlorantraniliprole
Spray into the whorl early morning or evening; act when >20% of young plants are damaged

pests.symptoms: Rows of small 'shot holes' across leaves, dead heart in young plants, tunnels and larvae inside stems, broken stalks.
cultural: Push-pull with desmodium and napier grass
Destroy or feed stalks to livestock after harvest
chemical: Registered granules or sprays applied to the whorl at first sign

pests.symptoms: Yellow-green mottling starting at the leaf base, leaf edges drying from the tip and margins inward, 'dead heart', small or no cobs, whole plants drying prematurely.
cultural: Uproot and destroy infected plants immediately
Plant certified seed only; do not recycle seed
Rotate out of maize for 1-2 seasons (beans, potatoes, cassava)
Avoid continuous or overlapping maize plantings
chemical: No cure. Control insect vectors (thrips, aphids) with registered insecticides early in the season

names.fr: Virus de la striure du maïs

pests.symptoms: Narrow, broken yellow-white streaks running along the leaf veins; stunted plants when infected early.
cultural: Plant early and avoid late plantings next to older maize
Remove grass weeds that host leafhoppers
chemical: Seed treatment against leafhopper vectors where recommended

pests.symptoms: Rectangular tan to grey lesions bounded by leaf veins, starting on lower leaves; common in humid, warm areas.
chemical: Strobilurin + triazole fungicide where the crop value justifies it

pests.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions (2.5-15 cm) on leaves, starting low on the plant in cool humid weather.
chemical: Triazole or strobilurin fungicide at early infection on susceptible varieties

pests.symptoms: Crop stunted and wilting/yellowing as if drought-stressed even with moisture; small plants with bright pink-purple flowers growing at the crop's base.
cultural: Uproot striga before it flowers and burn
Rotate with soybean, groundnut or cowpea
Add manure/compost; striga is worse on poor soils
biological: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. strigae (FOS) seed coating where available
chemical: Imazapyr-resistant (IR) maize with herbicide seed coating

pests.symptoms: Small holes in stored grain, flour-like dust, small dark beetles in the store.
cultural: Dry grain to 13% moisture (grain cracks when bitten)
Clean the store before new harvest
Use hermetic (airtight) storage bags or silos
chemical: Registered grain protectant dust (e.g. pirimiphos-methyl + permethrin) at label rates

pests.symptoms: Green-yellow or grey powdery mould on cobs or nuts, discoloured or shrivelled grain, musty smell.
cultural: Harvest on time and dry quickly off the ground (tarpaulin)
Sort out and destroy mouldy, damaged grain - never feed it to people or animals
Store dry in clean bags on pallets
biological: Aflasafe-type atoxigenic biocontrol applied 2-3 weeks before flowering

pests.symptoms: Small raised reddish-brown powdery pustules on the underside of leaves, often with a yellow halo.
chemical: Mancozeb preventively, or a triazole fungicide at first pustules

pests.symptoms: Angular grey-brown spots bounded by leaf veins; spots on pods are reddish-brown with dark borders.
chemical: Copper-based or mancozeb fungicides

pests.symptoms: Seedlings wilt and die; swollen, cracked stem base with small maggots or pupae inside; yellowing young plants.
cultural: Earth up soil around stems to encourage new roots
chemical: Insecticide seed dressing (e.g. thiamethoxam, imidacloprid)

pests.symptoms: Clusters of tiny soft green or black insects on shoot tips and leaf undersides, curled leaves, sticky honeydew, black sooty mould.
chemical: Systemic insecticides only as a last resort and not during flowering (protect bees)

pests.symptoms: Round exit holes in stored beans, small beetles in storage.
chemical: Registered storage protectant dust

pests.symptoms: Yellow/pale green mosaic patterns on leaves, distorted, twisted and reduced leaves, stunted plants.
cultural: Plant only clean cuttings from healthy plants
Uproot and destroy infected plants early
chemical: No cure

pests.symptoms: Yellow blotches along secondary leaf veins on older leaves, brown streaks on green stems, dry brown corky rot inside roots.
cultural: Uproot and destroy infected plants; report to extension
chemical: No cure

pests.symptoms: White waxy cotton-like insects on shoot tips, bunched 'bunchy top' leaves, shortened internodes.
biological: Parasitoid wasp Anagyrus lopezi (classical biological control)

pests.symptoms: Clouds of tiny white flying insects when leaves are disturbed, yellowing leaves, sticky honeydew; vectors of viruses.
chemical: Rotate registered insecticide groups to avoid resistance

pests.symptoms: Diamond/spindle-shaped lesions with grey centres and brown margins on leaves; blackened neck that breaks so panicles hang down white and empty.
chemical: Tricyclazole or other registered blast fungicides at booting/heading

pests.symptoms: Yellow-orange mottling and streaking of leaves, stunting, reduced tillering, poor panicle emergence.
cultural: Destroy stubble and volunteer rice between seasons
chemical: No cure

pests.symptoms: Dead central tiller ('dead heart') during tillering; white empty panicles ('white heads') at heading.
chemical: Registered insecticides when infestation exceeds thresholds

pests.symptoms: Large dark water-soaked patches on leaves and stems spreading fast in cool wet weather, white mould under leaves, firm brown greasy patches on fruit.
cultural: Remove and destroy infected plants and leaves
Water at the base, not the leaves
Do not plant next to potatoes
chemical: Mancozeb preventively in wet weather
Metalaxyl + mancozeb or other systemic once symptoms appear; rotate groups

pests.symptoms: Irregular whitish/transparent mines (blotches) in leaves with dark frass inside, holes in fruit, small caterpillars.
cultural: Remove and destroy infested leaves and fruits
chemical: Spinosad, emamectin benzoate or chlorantraniliprole; rotate modes of action

pests.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric 'target' rings on older lower leaves, yellowing around spots.
chemical: Mancozeb or chlorothalonil; azoxystrobin-based products

pests.symptoms: Sudden wilting of green plants in the heat of the day without yellowing; a cut stem placed in clear water releases milky white streams.
cultural: Uproot and destroy wilted plants (do not compost)
Rotate 3+ years away from tomato, potato, pepper, eggplant
Do not move soil or water from infected fields; disinfect tools
chemical: No effective chemical cure

names.fr: Mildiou de la pomme de terre

pests.symptoms: Dark brown-black water-soaked lesions on leaves with pale halo and white mould underneath in humid weather; brown rot in tubers.
cultural: Plant certified seed and tolerant varieties
Hill up well to protect tubers
Remove volunteer potatoes and cull piles
chemical: Preventive mancozeb sprays every 7-10 days in wet weather
Systemic + contact mixes after first symptoms

pests.symptoms: Severely stunted bushy plants with small, mottled, yellow or dark-green crinkled leaves.
cultural: Plant early and at close spacing
chemical: Control aphid vectors early

pests.symptoms: Orange-yellow powdery spots on the underside of leaves, leaf drop.
cultural: Resistant varieties (e.g. Ruiru 11, Batian in Kenya)
chemical: Copper fungicides preventively; triazoles curatively

pests.symptoms: Dark sunken lesions on green berries that turn black and drop; flower blossoms blackened.
chemical: Copper-based fungicides during rainy periods from flowering

pests.symptoms: Small round holes at the tip of berries, damaged beans with tunnels.
cultural: Pick all ripe, overripe and fallen berries (strip picking at season end)
chemical: Registered insecticides if infestation is high

pests.symptoms: Yellowing and wilting leaves, shrivelled male bud, uneven premature fruit ripening, yellow bacterial ooze from cut pseudostem, brown stains in fruit pulp.
cultural: Remove male buds with a forked stick
Disinfect tools with fire or bleach between plants
Cut down and bury infected mats (single diseased stem removal)
Use clean suckers; report to extension
chemical: No chemical cure

pests.symptoms: Older leaves yellow from the margins and collapse around the pseudostem, splitting at the base, reddish-brown discolouration inside the stem.
cultural: Do not move soil, plants or water from infected fields
chemical: No chemical cure

pests.symptoms: Tunnels in the corm, weak plants that topple, poor bunches, black weevils under trash.
cultural: Pare and hot-water treat suckers before planting
Chop and spread old pseudostems after harvest
